question.worked_solution:
We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{3}(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}) & = \\ (6{x}^{3})(\frac{x}{2})+(6{x}^{3})(-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}) & = \\ (6{x}^{3})(\frac{1}{2}x)+(6{x}^{3})(-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}) & = \\ (6\cdot \frac{1}{2})({x}^{3}\cdot x)+(6\cdot (-\frac{1}{3}))({x}^{3}\cdot {x}^{3}) & = \\ (3)({x}^{3+1})+(-2)\cdot ({x}^{3+3}) & = \\ 3{x}^{4}-2{x}^{6}\end{aligned}
$$
